title: EXAMPLE: The surprise prize message
summary: A short example story that shows every feature of the story engine. Replace with real, reviewed stories.

sources.title: FTC: How to Recognize and Report Spam Text Messages

kids.summary: A quick example story about a message that says you won a prize.

meters.label: Trust
meters.description: How much you believe the message

meters.label: What the scammer knows about you

intro.speaker: Unknown number
intro.text: CONGRATS! You won a $500 Brightmart gift card! Claim in the next 10 minutes or it goes to someone else: brightmart-prizes.example

kids.text: YOU WON 5,000 free gems for Starfall Quest! Claim in the next 10 minutes or they go to someone else. Tap here!

redFlags: A prize you never entered to win
A link from a number you don't know

choices.label: Tap the link to claim it
choices.redFlag: You never entered a contest, and the message gave you only 10 minutes. Real prizes don't rush you.
choices.lesson: Don't tap links in surprise prize messages. If you think it might be real, go to the company's website by typing the address yourself.

kids.lesson: Don't tap links in surprise prize messages. Show a grown-up you trust first.

choices.label: Ignore it and delete the message
choices.lesson: Exactly right. A surprise prize with a countdown is a classic trick.

form.speaker: Prize page
form.text: Almost there! Enter your full name, home address and phone number so we can send your prize.
redFlags: A prize page asking for personal details

choices.label: Fill in the form
choices.redFlag: The page wanted your name, address and phone number. Scammers collect these to trick you again or to pretend to be you.
choices.lesson: Close the page. Never type personal details into a page you reached from a surprise message.

choices.label: Something feels off. Close the page.
choices.lesson: Good instinct. Trust that 'something feels off' feeling.

end-good.text: You deleted the message and got on with your day. No prize, but no problem either.

ending.title: Not falling for it
ending.rewindSummary: You spotted the trick right away. Surprise prizes with a countdown are designed to make you hurry.

end-mixed.text: You closed the page before typing anything. The scammer knows your number works, so you might get more messages, but they got nothing else.

ending.title: A close call
ending.rewindSummary: Tapping the link told the scammer your number is real, but you stopped before sharing anything else.

end-bad.text: No gift card ever arrives. A week later, you start getting calls from people who know your name and address.

ending.title: The prize was the bait
ending.rewindSummary: The 'prize' was a way to collect your personal details. It happens to careful people too. That's why knowing the red flags helps.
